stories.headline: Sysco to Acquire Jetro Restaurant Depot for $29.1 Billion Including Debt

key_facts.fact: Sysco will acquire family-owned Jetro Restaurant Depot in a deal with a total enterprise value of approximately $29.1 billion, including debt, marking its entry into the cash-and-carry channel.
Restaurant Depot shareholders will receive $21.6 billion in cash and 91.5 million Sysco shares, giving them a roughly 16% stake in the combined company.
Sysco will fund the deal through $21 billion of new and hybrid debt plus $1 billion of cash and equity on hand, and will pause its share repurchase program.
Restaurant Depot operates a wholesale cash-and-carry model with about 166 warehouse locations across 35 U.S. states, complementing Sysco's delivery network.
Sysco shares fell about 5-8% in premarket trading on the news. The deal is expected to add mid- to high-single-digit EPS accretion in the first year after closing, expected by Q3 fiscal 2027.
Paul, Weiss is advising Sysco on the acquisition. Restaurant Depot was founded in Brooklyn in 1976 and is the nation's largest cash-and-carry wholesaler.
The deal follows failed merger talks last year between US Foods and Performance Food Group, which would have created a combined challenger to Sysco.

stories.headline: Eli Lilly and Insilico Medicine Sign $2.75 Billion AI Drug Discovery Deal

key_facts.fact: Insilico Medicine signed a global licensing and research deal with Eli Lilly worth up to $2.75 billion including milestone payments, with a $115 million upfront payment.
Lilly receives an exclusive worldwide license to develop, manufacture and commercialize preclinical oral drug candidates discovered by Insilico's AI, including a GLP-1 drug for diabetes.

Insilico has developed at least 28 drugs using generative AI, with nearly half already at clinical stage. The company went public in Hong Kong in December 2025 and its shares are up more than 50% year-to-date.
The two companies have collaborated since 2023, when they signed an AI-based software licensing agreement. Insilico will join Lilly's Gateway Labs community for biotech development.
The deal includes development, regulatory and commercial milestone payments plus tiered royalties on future sales, reflecting pharma's increasing turn to AI to accelerate R&D.

stories.headline: Amazon Acquires Fauna Robotics, Maker of Sprout Humanoid Robot

key_facts.fact: Amazon has acquired Fauna Robotics, a two-year-old New York startup that introduced the Sprout humanoid robot designed for social spaces like homes and schools.

Fauna was founded by former Meta and Google engineers: Josh Merel (Google DeepMind researcher) and Rob Cochran (former head of product at CTRL-Labs, the neural interface company Meta acquired in 2019).

Sprout is a 42-inch, 50-pound bipedal humanoid running on Nvidia's Jetson Orin platform, with a swappable 3-hour battery, priced at $50,000 for R&D partners. Early customers included Disney and Boston Dynamics.
Fauna raised at least $30 million from Kleiner Perkins, Quiet Capital and Lux Capital before the Amazon acquisition. The deal price was not disclosed.
Fauna joins Amazon's Personal Robotics Group, the same division that previously attempted and discontinued the Astro home robot in 2024 and abandoned the iRobot acquisition under regulatory pressure.

stories.headline: Aditya Birla-Blackstone Consortium Buys Royal Challengers Bengaluru for $1.78 Billion

key_facts.fact: A consortium comprising Aditya Birla Group, The Times of India Group, Bolt Ventures and Blackstone agreed to acquire 100% of Royal Challengers Bengaluru from United Spirits (Diageo subsidiary) for INR 166.6 billion (~$1.78 billion).
The deal includes both the men's IPL team and the women's WPL team. RCB won its first IPL title in 2025 and holds both IPL and Women's Premier League titles simultaneously.
Aryaman Vikram Birla will serve as Chairman and Satyan Gajwani as Vice Chairman of the franchise under the new ownership structure.
The transaction marks a strategic exit for United Spirits (Diageo) to sharpen focus on its core beverage alcohol business. The acquisition is subject to BCCI and CCI approvals.

stories.headline: Blackstone-Backed EPL to Merge with Indorama's Indovida in $2 Billion Packaging Deal

key_facts.fact: India's EPL Ltd agreed to merge with Indovida, backed by Thailand's Indorama Ventures, in a deal valuing the combined business at about $2 billion. EPL is valued at ~$1.2 billion and Indovida at ~$700 million.
Post-merger, Indorama Ventures will become co-promoter with a 51.8% stake, while Blackstone (EPL's backer) will hold about 16.6% of the combined entity.
The merged group will combine EPL's packaging operations with Indovida's plastics portfolio. EPL is implied at 339 Indian rupees per share. The deal is expected to close within about a year.

stories.headline: Garanti BBVA Sells Romania Banking Unit to Raiffeisen Bank for €591 Million

key_facts.fact: Turkey-based Garanti (85% owned by Spain's BBVA) signed a €591 million ($682 million) deal to sell its Romania operations to Austria's Raiffeisen Bank International.
The deal transfers full shares in Garanti Bank S.A. and Motoractive IFN S.A. and is expected to close in Q4 2026, subject to regulatory approvals.
Garanti's Romanian unit has 67 branches, 1,118 employees and total assets of approximately $5.17 billion. It has operated in Romania since 1998.
The acquisition will make Raiffeisen the third-largest bank in Romania by total assets. RBI's Romanian subsidiaries currently hold €17.5 billion ($20.2 billion) in assets.

stories.headline: Vedanta Confirms April Timeline to Split Into Five Listed Companies

key_facts.fact: Vedanta chairman Anil Agarwal confirmed that the company, with an enterprise value of $37 billion, will split into five separately listed entities starting in April 2026.
The demerger, reported by the Financial Times, will create five standalone listed companies from one of India's largest natural resources conglomerates.
The restructuring has been planned for several years but faced multiple hurdles. Agarwal's confirmation of the April timeline represents a firm commitment to proceed.

stories.headline: Boardwalk Pipelines to Acquire Spire Marketing Gas Unit for $215 Million

key_facts.fact: Boardwalk Pipelines entered an agreement to acquire Spire Marketing Inc., a gas marketing business unit, from Spire Inc. (NYSE: SR) for $215 million.
The acquisition expands Boardwalk's presence across the natural gas value chain, adding Spire Marketing's established commercial and trading capabilities.
Spire is divesting the unit to sharpen focus on core regulated utility operations, simplify its business mix, and improve its risk profile. The deal is expected to close in Q2 2026.
Barclays served as financial advisor and GableGotwals as legal counsel to Boardwalk in the transaction.

stories.headline: Austria Delays FDI Clearance for JD.com's $2.5 Billion Takeover of Ceconomy

key_facts.fact: Austrian regulators have not approved Chinese e-commerce giant JD.com's proposed acquisition of German electronics retailer Ceconomy (owner of MediaMarkt and Saturn), putting the deal at risk.
Ceconomy said the Austrian Federal Ministry of Economy has raised concerns and refused to engage in a joint solution-finding process, despite FDI clearances already obtained in France and Italy.
Austria's economy ministry denied on March 30 that it was being obstructive, insisting it was cooperating on the deal review.
The investment agreement between Ceconomy and JD.com was signed on July 30, 2025. JD.com had committed to safeguards on locations, employment, data protection and management independence.

stories.headline: Federal Judge Halts $6.2B Nexstar-Tegna Integration After Antitrust Challenge

key_facts.fact: US District Judge Troy L. Nunley in Sacramento granted DirecTV's request to pause Nexstar-Tegna post-merger integration, even though the deal had already closed days earlier.
The combined entity would control 265 full-power television stations reaching approximately 80% of US households, though Nexstar has agreed to divest six stations at FCC request.
Judge Nunley noted the companies 'do not contest this merger will increase Nexstar's bargaining leverage to extract higher fees' for retransmission rates charged to cable and satellite providers.
The court ordered the companies to maintain and operate Tegna's business as independent, economically viable, and active competitors while the legal challenge proceeds.
A coalition of states led by California and New York also sued, pointing to 13 overlapping markets where the combined entity would control over 30% of retransmission revenue.
A hearing is scheduled for April 7 to determine whether the pause should remain in place pending a full trial.

stories.headline: DOJ Issues Subpoenas in $110B Paramount-Warner Bros. Discovery Merger Probe

key_facts.fact: The US Department of Justice has begun issuing subpoenas as part of its investigation into the proposed $110 billion acquisition involving Paramount Skydance and Warner Bros. Discovery.
DOJ investigators are examining how the combined company would influence studio output, content rights ownership, and streaming competition, plus downstream effects on movie theaters.
Acting Assistant Attorney General Omeed Assefi said Paramount will 'absolutely not' be fast-tracked for approval due to political considerations.
The European Commission has reportedly begun engaging with third parties, while Canadian authorities and the California Attorney General's office are also consulting industry participants.
Paramount has committed to paying Warner Bros. shareholders a quarterly 'ticking fee' of 25 cents per share starting in October if the deal remains incomplete.
Paramount projected approximately $6 billion in cost synergies from the merger; the Teamsters union warned the deal 'poses a direct threat' to employment.

stories.headline: RTL Offers EU Remedies to Fast-Track Sky Deutschland Takeover Approval

key_facts.fact: RTL is preparing to offer remedies to the European Commission to secure early approval for its planned acquisition of Sky Deutschland, with possible concessions including outsourcing advertising sales to third parties.

If remedies are submitted, the Commission's preliminary review deadline would be extended by 10 working days beyond the current April 8, 2026 deadline, with approval likely at the end of the initial review.
The acquisition would combine major sports rights including Bundesliga, Premier League, and Formula 1, and strengthen RTL's streaming position through Sky's WOW service.
German media regulator KEK cleared the transaction in September 2025, concluding combined audience share remained below thresholds indicating dominant opinion power.
RTL Group reported 2025 revenue of €6.0 billion, with streaming revenue rising 26% to €509 million and 8.1 million paying subscribers (+19%).

stories.headline: Sysco Strikes $29.1B Deal for Jetro Restaurant Depot, Faces Antitrust Scrutiny

key_facts.fact: Sysco announced a $29.1 billion deal to acquire Jetro Restaurant Depot in cash and stock, with Restaurant Depot shareholders receiving $21.6 billion in cash and 91.5 million Sysco shares.
The deal values Restaurant Depot at 14.6x operating income; the company operates 166 warehouse stores in 35 states generating $16 billion in annual revenue and $2.1 billion in EBITDA.
The combined company would generate nearly $100 billion in annual revenue and $6.4 billion in adjusted EBITDA, with $250 million in annual cost synergies projected within three years.
Sysco plans to fund the cash component with $21 billion in new debt and $1 billion in cash on hand; Restaurant Depot shareholders will own about 16% of Sysco stock post-close.
Restaurant Depot serves approximately 725,000 independent restaurant operators annually; Sysco plans to leverage its scale to open more than 125 new Restaurant Depot locations.

stories.headline: UK CMA Unveils 2026/27 Plan With Major Merger Control Reset

key_facts.fact: The CMA will 'step back' in global mergers to avoid unnecessary duplication with international counterparts and will be open to accepting behavioral remedies, a significant shift from prior reluctance.

Structural reform of the merger control process is planned, including replacing the independent Phase 2 panel with sub-committees of the CMA board comprising executives, non-executives, and industry experts.
The CMA plans to clarify share of supply (25%) and hybrid (33%) tests to limit its discretion with a closed set of specified statutory criteria for asserting jurisdiction.
The CMA is escalating enforcement against bid-rigging in public procurement, leveraging AI and data science to scan bidding data, with cartelists now facing debarment under the Procurement Act 2023.
The CMA has completed its first Strategic Market Status designations for search and mobile platforms under the Digital Markets, Competition and Consumers Act.

stories.headline: Naver-Dunamu Merger Delayed Three Months Amid Korean Antitrust Review

key_facts.fact: Naver disclosed on March 30 that the shareholder meeting for the share exchange between subsidiary Naver Financial and Dunamu (operator of Upbit, Korea's largest crypto exchange) has been postponed from May 22 to August 18, with deal closing pushed from June 30 to September 30.

Korea's Fair Trade Commission accepted the merger filing in November 2025 and is closely examining market dominance and monopoly concerns as the deal combines leaders in mobile payments and cryptocurrency markets.
The FTC review deadline was extended after the commission recently requested additional materials from both companies.

The Digital Asset Basic Act, being pushed by the government and ruling party, would limit major shareholder stakes in crypto exchanges to 20%, or up to 34% with Financial Services Commission approval.
Naver stated the content of the Digital Asset Basic Act 'once enacted and enforced could potentially affect the progress or outcome of this comprehensive share exchange.'

stories.headline: FCC Warns NFL's Streaming Shift May Threaten Its Antitrust Exemption

key_facts.fact: FCC Chairman Brendan Carr warned the NFL's increasing shift toward paid streaming platforms may challenge the league's antitrust exemption under the Sports Broadcasting Act of 1961.

The Sports Broadcasting Act of 1961 allows the NFL to negotiate TV rights collectively, but was crafted for free over-the-air broadcasts — creating a legal gray area for cable, satellite, and streaming.
Carr warned there may be a 'tipping point' where placing too many games behind paywalls could undermine the exemption entirely.
The NFL is negotiating future media rights deals, including CBS contracts that could extend beyond 2029 at higher fees than the current $2.1 billion annual agreement.
Thursday night NFL games are already carried exclusively on Amazon Prime Video, with speculation that more high-profile games could migrate to streaming.

stories.headline: Elliott Wins Board Overhaul at Norwegian Cruise Line Holdings

key_facts.fact: Norwegian Cruise Line Holdings entered a cooperation agreement with Elliott Investment Management, resulting in a full reconstitution of the board of directors.
Four long-standing board members will resign effective March 31, replaced by five new independent directors selected jointly by the company and Elliott.
The new CEO will also assume the role of chairman; the board will increase to nine directors, eight of whom qualify as independent.
New directors include former executives from British Airways and Disney Experiences, plus CEOs of a technology company and an investment firm.
Elliott had previously criticized the company for 'excellent ships but poor strategy execution and high costs' and expressed confidence the new board would restore investor confidence.

stories.headline: Indorama Ventures Merges with Blackstone-Backed EPL in $2B India Packaging Deal

key_facts.fact: Indorama Ventures will merge with Blackstone-backed EPL Limited to create a $2 billion packaging entity, with EPL valued at approximately $1.2 billion — a 70% premium over its closing stock price.
Upon completion, Indorama Ventures will hold 51.8% of the merged company, following its earlier 24.9% investment in EPL in February 2025.
The merger is part of IVL's 'IVL 2.0' strategy emphasizing value creation and market consolidation in India's packaging market, projected to reach $92 billion by FY30.
The deal is expected to close within 12 months pending regulatory approvals.

stories.headline: Blackstone-Led Consortium Acquires Royal Challengers Bengaluru for $1.78B

key_facts.fact: A consortium of Aditya Birla Group, Times of India Group, Bolt Ventures, and Blackstone agreed to acquire 100% of Royal Challengers Bengaluru from United Spirits (Diageo subsidiary) for INR 166.6 billion (~$1.78 billion).
The deal includes both the men's IPL team and the women's WPL team; RCB won its first IPL title in 2025.
Aryaman Vikram Birla will serve as Chairman and Satyan Gajwani as Vice Chairman of the franchise under the new ownership.
The transaction marks a strategic shift for United Spirits as it focuses on its core beverage alcohol business under Diageo.

stories.headline: Advent International Commits $1B to Defense Tech, Co-Leads Shield AI $1.5B Round

key_facts.fact: Advent International announced a commitment to invest up to $1 billion in next-generation defense technology companies, building on over $15 billion deployed in the defense sector since 2020.
As its initial investment, Advent signed a definitive agreement to co-lead Shield AI's $1.5 billion Series G round, which values the company at $12.7 billion.
Shield AI, founded in 2015, develops AI-powered autonomous systems for air operations; the transaction is expected to close in Q2 2026.
Advent's prior defense investments include Cobham, Ultra Electronics, Vantor, and Attalon.

stories.headline: Motorola Solutions to Buy Bell's Land Mobile Radio Business for C$675M

key_facts.fact: Motorola Solutions will acquire Bell Mobility's land mobile radio (LMR) network business for C$675 million, expected to close in Q4 2026 pending regulatory approval.
Bell and Motorola have co-managed secure radio networks serving Canadian emergency services and businesses for over 30 years.
Bell will remain as a key service delivery partner even after transferring the network assets to Motorola.
